AD-100 at a glance

The AD-100 is a remotely operated dredging robot for removing sediment from hydropower sumps and other confined submerged spaces. Manufacturer figures: 100 kg vehicle, 815 × 620 × 690 mm, six thrusters and front and rear cameras. It works as one system with a pump, discharge line and mud-water separation unit.

FAQ

AD-100 questions.

Where is the AD-100 used?

The manufacturer brochure describes underwater sump dredging at hydropower facilities. Other tanks and confined spaces need an access, geometry and sediment review.

What is the AD-100 dredging rate?

No verified net removal rate is published. The brochure’s 5 m³/h figure is the capacity of the paired mud-water separation equipment, not the robot’s sediment-removal rate.

Does the sump need to be drained?

The AD-100 is a remotely operated underwater platform, so sediment can be removed with the robot submerged rather than by draining and manual entry. Confirm this for your sump, together with discharge, treatment and site permissions.

How do I get a price for the AD-100?

Price depends on the configuration: sensors, tether length, tools and support equipment. Send a short project brief or email us, and we will reply with the questions needed for an itemised quotation.
